- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment, leading to overshoots in subsequent days; dampen forecast after spike.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early days of the 30d horizon; model should anchor closer to recent 7-14 day average for medium-term.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to adjust downward quickly; apply downward correction with lagged sentiment signal.
- For 30d horizon, model underestimates downward trends after strong negative sentiment; add 1-2% buffer to forecast when sentiment is negative and price is falling.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high sentiment days; if sentiment is positive for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
